question: What is the minimum attendance required to appear for the end-semester examination?
answer: A student must have a minimum of 75 per cent attendance in each course, computed separately for the theory and practical components, in order to be eligible to appear for the end-semester examination in that course. Attendance is counted from the first day of instruction of the semester to the last instructional day and includes all lectures, tutorials and practical sessions scheduled for the course.

question: How are marks split between internal assessment and the end-semester exam for a theory course?
answer: For a theory course, the total evaluation is for 100 marks, split into 40 marks for continuous internal assessment and 60 marks for the end-semester examination conducted by the Controller of Examinations. The 40 internal-assessment marks themselves consist of two mid-term tests of 15 marks each (held in the 6th and 12th weeks) plus 10 marks for assignments, quizzes or tutorials.

question: What is the minimum I need to score to pass a course?
answer: To pass a course, you must score at least 30% in the end-semester examination AND at least 40% of the total marks (internal assessment plus end-semester examination combined). If you fail to meet either of these requirements, you will be awarded an 'F' grade in that course.

question: What letter grade do I get for 85 marks?
answer: For 85 marks out of 100, you will receive the letter grade A+ (Excellent) with 9 grade points, since 85 falls within the 80 to 89 marks range.

question: How many days do I have to apply for re-evaluation after results are declared?
answer: You must apply for re-evaluation to the Controller of Examinations within ten working days of the declaration of results, along with the prescribed fee per course. No application will be entertained after this period. Note that re-evaluation is only available for end-semester theory courses and not for practical examinations, project evaluations, or internal assessment.

question: What happens if I miss an end-semester exam because I was ill?
answer: If you miss an end-semester exam due to illness, you must submit a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner, countersigned by the Institute Medical Officer, to the Controller of Examinations within five working days of the exam date. On acceptance of the certificate, you will be allowed to appear for the course in the next supplementary examination, and that appearance will be treated as your first attempt — exempt from the supplementary examination fee.

question: What is the penalty if I am caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall?
answer: If you are caught with a mobile phone in the examination hall, it is treated as a first offence under the Unfair Means rules. Under EE §4.2, a first offence leads to cancellation of that course's examination and the award of a grade F in that course; a second offence cancels all examinations of the semester with grade F in every course; and a third offence leads to expulsion from the Institute. Note that possession alone, even if the phone is switched off, counts as the first offence.

question: What time do the hostel gates close at night?
answer: The hostel gates close at 10:30 p.m. every day, and the gates reopen at 5:30 a.m.

question: Can I use an induction cooktop in my hostel room?
answer: No. The Hostel Handbook explicitly prohibits the use of induction cooktops in hostel rooms, along with other appliances such as electric heaters, immersion rods, electric kettles, and irons, as well as any appliance rated above 500 watts. Using one will lead to confiscation of the appliance and a fine of Rs. 1,000 for each occurrence.

question: How much is the late fee if I pay my semester fees after the due date?
answer: If you pay your semester fees after the due date, a late fee of Rs. 100 per day is charged on any fee paid after the due date, up to and including the last date shown in the schedule. The late fee is capped at Rs. 1,500 for any single payment.

question: What is the last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee?
answer: The last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee (along with the examination and development fee) is 31 July 2026. After this date, fees are not accepted unless the Registrar grants a special written permission within five working days on the ground of a documented delay in an education loan or scholarship disbursement.

question: Who is eligible for the merit-cum-means scholarship?
answer: You are eligible for the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship if your annual family income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000 and you have a CGPA of not less than 7.0 at the end of the preceding academic year (or, for first-year students, not less than 80 per cent marks in the qualifying examination). The scholarship is a waiver of twenty-five per cent of the tuition fee, and you must attach an income certificate from a Tehsildar or equivalent officer, not older than six months, with your application.

question: Do I get leave if there is a death in my family?
answer: Yes, you are entitled to bereavement leave if a parent, sibling, grandparent, or spouse passes away. You may be granted up to seven days of leave, which will be counted as attendance. You must inform the HoD by e-mail or through the student portal before or during the leave, and submit a written application on your return.

question: Will I get my hall ticket if I have not paid my tuition fees?
answer: No, you will not be issued a hall ticket if you have outstanding tuition fee dues on the last date of payment. The hall ticket will be released only within one working day after you clear the dues, provided the examination has not yet commenced. Additionally, your registration remains provisional until the fees are paid in full, and the hall ticket is issued only if you have no outstanding tuition fee dues.

question: How long can a break of study be?
answer: A break of study may be permitted for one semester or one academic year, and only on medical grounds certified by the Institute Medical Officer and approved by the Dean. A break of study shall not be granted more than once during the programme.

question: What is the maximum time allowed to complete the B.Tech programme?
answer: The maximum time allowed to complete the B.Tech programme is seven academic years from the date of first admission. If a student fails to finish all requirements within this period, their name shall be removed from the rolls of the Institute.

question: Can I get a mess rebate if I go home for two weeks?
answer: Yes, you are entitled to a mess rebate for a two-week absence. HH §4.3 provides that a resident absent from the hostel for a continuous period of seven days or more gets a rebate of mess charges for the period of absence, provided the absence is recorded in the leave register in advance and the rebate form is submitted within seven days of return. Two weeks clearly exceeds the seven-day minimum, so make sure you log your leave in advance and file the rebate form within seven days of coming back.

question: How much medical insurance cover do students have?
answer: Every student is covered under the Institute's group medical insurance scheme for hospitalisation expenses of up to Rs. 1,00,000 per year. The premium is included in the development fee, and claims must be made through the Institute Medical Officer within thirty days of discharge from the hospital.

question: My attendance is 58% because I was hospitalised for three weeks. Can the shortage be condoned?
answer:
The rulebook gives two incompatible condonation thresholds on medical grounds, and your 58% attendance falls between them.

AR §4.3 says: 'A shortage of attendance below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances,' which would forbid condonation in your case.

LM §2.2 says: 'the shortfall may be condoned by the Dean … provided that the student's overall attendance in the course is not less than 55 per cent,' which would permit condonation since 58% is above 55%.

Because the two clauses disagree on the very threshold for medical condonation, the rulebook itself does not tell you which one applies to your situation.

question: What is the lowest attendance percentage that can still be condoned on medical grounds?
answer: Two passages give different minimum attendance thresholds for medical condonation. [LM §2.2] permits condonation provided the student's overall attendance in the course is not less than 55 per cent. [AR §4.3] permits condonation only if attendance in the course concerned is not less than 65 per cent, and expressly states that a shortage below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances. Because these two clauses set incompatible floors for the same situation, you should treat the question as unresolved under the passages as presented and seek clarification from the Dean / Academic Office.

question: If I withdraw my admission before classes begin, how much of my tuition fee will be refunded?
answer: Two passages give incompatible figures for refund of tuition fee when admission is withdrawn before classes begin. [SF §6.2] says the tuition fee shall be refunded only after deduction of a 10% processing charge, i.e. you get back 90% of the tuition fee. [FS §4.1] says a student who withdraws before commencement of classes shall be refunded 100% of the tuition fee. These two rules cannot both apply to the same situation.

question: What CGPA do I need to maintain to keep my merit scholarship?
answer: There is a direct disagreement between the two clauses on the CGPA required to keep the Merit Scholarship. AR §11.2 states the Merit Scholarship continues provided the student maintains a CGPA of not less than 7.5 at the end of each semester. SF §3.1 states the Merit Scholarship continues only if the student maintains a CGPA of not less than 8.0 at the end of each semester. The clauses disagree on the threshold number itself, so the rulebook as provided does not give a single consistent answer.

question: What happens if I miss the end-semester exam because of a family wedding?
answer: The Examination and Evaluation Regulations do not address what happens if a student misses an end-semester exam because of a family wedding; the rules supplied only cover absence on medical grounds. You should contact the Controller of Examinations to find out whether any concession applies, but nothing in the supplied passages grants or denies it. The closest passage, EE §3.1, covers absence due to illness, not personal or family events.

question: Can I get a re-test if I missed a mid-term test for a job interview?
answer: The rulebook does not address a re-test for a mid-term test missed because of a job interview. The closest provision, [EE §3.3], only permits a re-test when the mid-term test is missed on medical grounds with a certificate submitted within five working days.

question: Can I change my branch after the first year?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student may change their branch after the first year. None of the supplied passages cover branch transfer or branch change; the closest provision is the academic regulation governing promotion to the next year based on credits earned.

question: Is there a dress code for laboratory sessions?
answer: The rulebook supplied to me does not address whether students must follow a dress code during laboratory sessions. The closest passage covers laboratory records and admission to the practical examination, not attire.

question: Can a day scholar eat in the hostel mess by paying per meal?
answer: The Hostel Handbook does not address whether a day scholar can eat in the hostel mess by paying per meal. The closest passage simply requires every resident to be a member of the hostel mess and to pay mess charges in advance for the semester.

question: Are pets allowed in the hostel?
answer: The hostel rules supplied do not address whether pets are allowed in the hostel. The closest passage is the list of prohibited activities and items, which mentions alcohol, tobacco, drugs, gambling, loud music, firecrackers, posters, and overnight guests, but says nothing about pets.

question: What is the fee for a duplicate identity card?
answer: The rulebook does not address the fee for a duplicate identity card. The closest passage, EE §1.2, only mentions the Institute identity card as something a student must carry to be admitted to the examination hall, but does not specify any charge for a duplicate.

question: Can I get academic credit for a summer internship?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a summer internship can earn academic credit. The closest passage, AR §2.2, only explains how credits are assigned to courses (lectures, tutorials, practicals) and that 160 credits are required for the B.Tech. degree; it does not mention internships.

question: Is there a scholarship for students from the EWS category?
answer: The rulebook does not address any scholarship specifically for students of the EWS (Economically Weaker Section) category. The closest passage covers the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship, which is based on family income and academic performance, not on EWS category status.

question: Are grace marks given if I fail a course by one or two marks?
answer: The rulebook does not address the question of grace marks being given to a student who fails a course by one or two marks. None of the passages mention grace marks, and the closest passage, AR §5.4, only states the passing requirement of 30 per cent in the end-semester exam and 40 per cent overall, with the grade 'F' awarded otherwise.

question: Can I use a scientific calculator in the examination hall?
answer: A scientific calculator is not listed among the items you are permitted to bring into the examination hall under the Examination and Evaluation Regulations. You may only bring your hall ticket, Institute identity card, blue or black ball-point pens, pencils, an eraser, a transparent water bottle, and any other item expressly permitted on the question paper. Unless the specific question paper expressly permits a calculator, do not bring one, as prohibited electronic items (communication devices) are banned and possession can amount to use of unfair means.

question: What happens if there is a printing error in the question paper?
answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if there is a printing error in the question paper. The closest passage is EE §6.2, which deals with the correction of clerical errors in provisional results within sixty days of their declaration.

question: How do I get a duplicate degree certificate if I lose the original?
answer: The rulebook does not address how to obtain a duplicate degree certificate if the original is lost. The closest passage covers only the requirement that the original degree certificate is issued only after a no-dues certificate is obtained from the Library, Hostel Office, Department, and Finance Office, but it says nothing about re-issuement of a lost certificate.

question: How many books can I borrow from the library at a time?
answer: The rulebook does not address the number of books a student may borrow from the library at one time. The closest passage merely requires obtaining a no-dues clearance from the Library before certain certificates are issued.

question: What is the procedure to transfer to another university mid-course?
answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure for transferring to another university mid-course. The closest passage concerns what happens when a student withdraws from the programme, including the submission of a withdrawal form to the Registrar and the need for a no-dues certificate before documents are released.

question: Can I keep a two-wheeler in the hostel parking?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether residents may keep a two-wheeler in the hostel parking. The closest passage is HH §5.4, which lists other prohibited activities and items but says nothing about vehicles or parking.

question: Is there a fee concession if my sibling also studies at the institute?
answer: The rulebook does not address a fee concession based on a sibling studying at the Institute. The closest passage covers a concession for children of permanent Institute staff, not for siblings of enrolled students.

question: Will I get my hall ticket if my hostel fee is unpaid but my tuition fee is paid?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether an unpaid hostel fee (with tuition fee paid) will prevent you from receiving your hall ticket. The closest passages cover only outstanding tuition fee dues: under AR §12.2 a student with outstanding tuition fee dues on the last date of payment shall not be issued a hall ticket, and under EE §1.2 hall tickets are issued to students with no outstanding tuition fee dues — neither rule mentions hostel fees.

question: What is the minimum CGPA to be eligible for campus placements?
answer: The rulebook does not address the minimum CGPA required to be eligible for campus placements. The closest passage discusses a different CGPA threshold for registering additional credits.

question: Can I re-appear in a course I have already passed to improve my grade?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student may re-appear in a course already passed in order to improve the grade. The closest provision, AR §9.1, deals only with re-evaluation of an answer script after results are declared.

question: What happens if I fall ill in the middle of writing an exam?
answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if you fall ill in the middle of writing an exam (for example, whether you may leave the hall, get a make-up paper, or have your paper treated specially). The closest passage deals with missing a mid-term test on medical grounds, not falling ill during an exam you are actually taking.

question: How do I get my name corrected on the grade card?
answer: The rulebook does not address how to get a name corrected on the grade card. The closest passage covers the issuance of grade cards and provisional results, stating that results are provisional until the grade card is issued and are subject to correction of clerical errors by the Controller of Examinations within sixty days.

question: Can I audit a course without earning credits?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student may audit a course without earning credits. The closest passage is AR §3.1, which covers the general requirement that every student must register for courses at the beginning of each semester, but it does not mention auditing or non-credit enrolment.

question: Is the examination fee refunded if I withdraw from an exam?
answer: No. The examination fee is not refundable after the commencement of classes, including in the event of withdrawal.

question: What is the punishment for plagiarism in a project report?
answer: The rulebook does not address the specific punishment for plagiarism in a project report. The closest passage covers unfair means in examinations generally, not plagiarism in submitted project reports.
